issues.failure_explanation: The proof of Proposition prop:norm_bub bounds |b-Pi_kappa b|_{1,K} by C|b-Pi_kappa b|_{1/2,partial K} citing the lifting theorem. A lifting theorem only provides some extension of boundary data with controlled energy; it cannot bound the energy of a given function by its boundary seminorm (for arbitrary functions this is false: interior oscillations with zero trace have zero boundary seminorm but positive H^1 seminorm; the harmonic lifting in fact minimizes energy, i.e. gives the opposite inequality). The inequality is true here only because b-Pi_kappa b ranges over a finite-dimensional VEM-type space on which the boundary seminorm is actually a norm (via unisolvence of the bubble degrees of freedom: zero boundary seminorm forces Pi_kappa b to vanish on the boundary, and then b=Pi_kappa b), with mesh-uniform constants by scaling -- a nontrivial finite-dimensional norm-equivalence argument that is entirely missing. The identical defective inference recurs in the proof of Proposition prop:added-3, where |vtilde-Pi_k vtilde|_{1,K} <= C|vtilde-Pi_k vtilde|_{1/2,partial K} is attributed to the trace theorem, which states the reverse direction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add a lemma proving that on the finite-dimensional spaces {b-Pi_kappa b : b in bubble_kappa(K)} and {vtilde-Pi_k vtilde : vtilde in enhanced_k(K)} the H^{1/2}(boundary K) seminorm is a norm that bounds the H^1(K) seminorm (via unisolvence of the VEM degrees of freedom), with constants uniform over shape-regular meshes satisfying G1-G2 by a scaling/compactness argument.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:norm_bub (self-stability of bubbles) is not established as written. It underlies the stable splitting prop:added-3, the stability/continuity of a_h in prop:stab (including the beta_sharp=0 variant adopted in the numerical tests) and prop:cont-cor, and through them the well-posedness results prop:added-7 and thm:added-2 and all error estimates thm:est, cor:added-1, thm:added-3.
issues.title: Unjustified energy-by-trace inequality in the bubble self-stability proof (also reused for the splitting stability)
issues.why_classification: The statements are correct and the repair is a contained but nontrivial new lemma (finite-dimensional norm equivalence with uniform constants); once supplied, every downstream claim, rate, and the advertised scope survive unchanged, so it is more than a routine local fix but requires no new global proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: The only justification offered for the unisolvence of the velocity degrees of freedom is the claim that the local velocity space is contained in [enhanced_{k+2}(K)]^2. This inclusion is false: membership in the enhanced space of degree k+2 requires (v - Pi_{k+2} v, m) = 0 for all m in monomials_{k+2}\monomials_k, but for a generic sum vtilde+d (e.g. a non-polynomial virtual bubble d in bubbleS) the moments against monomials_{k+2}\monomials_k are not prescribed by the construction and do not coincide with those of Pi_{k+2}(vtilde+d). The inclusion does hold for the enlarged space Z_{k+2}(K) (boundary in P_{k+2}, Laplacian in P_k subset P_{k+2}), not for the enhanced one. The unisolvence statement itself is true but is left without a valid argument.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove unisolvence directly: if all DOFs dofs(v)#1-#4 vanish, then the enhanced-space DOFs of vtilde vanish (the bubble part is L^2-orthogonal to P_{k-2} and vanishes on the boundary), hence vtilde=0 by enhanced-space unisolvence, and then the bubble moments vanish, hence d=0 by bubble unisolvence; together with the stated dimension count this gives the result.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition prop:added-4 (unisolvence of the velocity DOFs, on which the whole DOF-based construction of the MINI-VEM rests) has no valid proof as written; no other labelled result cites it.
issues.title: False inclusion V_k(K) subset [enhanced_{k+2}(K)]^2 used as justification of DOF unisolvence
issues.why_classification: The unisolvence result is true and a short, routine direct proof repairs the defect; no claim, rate, or scope is lost and no nontrivial new lemma is needed.

issues.failure_explanation: From the preceding bound a_h^K(v,v) <= C^star[a^K(vtilde,vtilde)+a^K(d,d)] (with C^star=max{1,alpha^star,beta_sharp gamma^star}, using the Pythagoras identities of eq:pezzi_ah), the proof adds and subtracts 2a^K(vtilde,d) to form C^star a^K(v,v), but writes the residual as -a^K(Q_k vtilde,d) instead of the correct -2C^star a^K(vtilde,d) = -2C^star a^K(Q_k vtilde,d), and then concludes a_h^K(v,v) <= C^star a^K(v,v) by dropping this residual. The dropped term has no sign: a^K(Q_k vtilde,d)=a^K(vtilde,d) is not >= 0 in general (it changes sign if d is replaced by -d). Hence the continuity (upper) inequality of eq:stab is not proved as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Stop the estimate at a_h^K(v,v) <= max{1,alpha^star,beta_sharp gamma^star}[a^K(vtilde,vtilde)+a^K(d,d)] and invoke the stable splitting of Proposition prop:added-3, which yields a_h^K(v,v) <= max{1,alpha^star,beta_sharp gamma^star} eta^{-2} a^K(v,v).
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound of eq:stab, hence the continuity of a_h asserted in prop:cont-cor and used throughout the well-posedness (prop:added-7, thm:added-2) and error analysis (thm:est, cor:added-1, thm:added-3), is not established as written.
issues.title: Upper bound in the stability proof of a_h drops a cross term of indefinite sign
issues.why_classification: The stability statement is true and the repair is a short, local, routine replacement of the final lines of the proof using an already-stated proposition (prop:added-3); every claim and constant type survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed claim asserts delta_star||q_h||_0^2 <= c_h(q_h,q_h) for all q_h in Q_k. This is false: c_h only sees the non-polynomial part Qzero{k}q_h = q_h - Pizero{k}q_h, so for any nonzero piecewise-polynomial pressure (e.g. q_h = x - 1/2 on (0,1)^2, which lies in Q_k subset L^2_0 for k>=1) one has Pizero{k}q_h = q_h and therefore c_h(q_h,q_h)=0 while ||q_h||_0>0. Summing the hypothesis eq:stab_sp (which holds only on ker(Pizero{k})) yields only delta_star||Qzero{k}q_h||_0^2 <= c_h(q_h,q_h) <= delta^star||Qzero{k}q_h||_0^2; the word 'Thus' overgeneralizes the bound to the full L^2 norm and materially misstates what the stabilization controls (the non-polynomial pressure contribution only -- the very reason c_h is needed in addition to the bubbles).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace ||q_h||_{0,Omega} by ||Qzero{k}q_h||_{0,Omega} on both sides of the display, matching eq:stab_sp summed over the mesh.
issues.overall_effect: The stated coercivity property of the pressure stabilization is false. No subsequent labelled argument uses the strong form (the weak inf-sup proof in prop:added-6 uses the correct ker(Pizero{k}) version through eq:stab_sp), so the formal analysis is unaffected once the display is corrected.
issues.title: Pressure stabilization c_h is falsely claimed to be coercive on the whole of Q_k
issues.why_classification: The correction withdraws a substantive (though unused) promise, so it is not a pure typo, but it is a strictly local statement fix: no inference in the paper depends on the false strong version, and all results survive unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $v\in \mathrm{H}^{k+1}(\elementvem)$, the following optimal order error estimate holds true
which, together with a standard inverse inequality and~\eqref{eq:norm_equal}, gives

issues.failure_explanation: The proof takes v(q_h) in V = [H^1_0(Omega)]^2 from the surjectivity of the divergence and defines v_I as its nodal/moment VEM interpolant. (i) For a general H^1 function the nodal degrees of freedom (vertex and edge point values) are not defined. (ii) Even for smooth v(q_h), the absorption step 'a standard inverse inequality and (eq:norm_equal)' uses ||v_I||_1 <= C||v(q_h)||_1 and ||v(q_h)-v_I||_0 <= Ch||v(q_h)||_1 (to turn epsilon||v_I||_1^2 and epsilon h^{-2}||v-v_I||_0^2 into epsilon||q_h||_0^2); nodal interpolation satisfies no such first-order estimates in the H^1 norm alone -- the paper's own interpolation results (prop:added-1, prop:interp_enh) require H^{k+1} regularity and yield h^{k+1}||v||_{k+1} (e.g. a function equal to 1 in the interior but vanishing at all vertices has arbitrarily small H^1 seminorm while its L^2 distance to its k=1 interpolant, which is zero, stays O(1)). (iii) The H^1 norm of the bubble-corrected velocity v_h = v_I + d_h is never estimated, although the statement asserts ||v_h||_1 = ||q_h||_0.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Choose v(q_h) as a regularized divergence (Bogovskii-type) lifting of q_h in H^1(Omega) with ||v||_j <= C||q_h||_{j-1}, j=1,2, rescaled so that ||v||_1=||q_h||_0; then |v|_2 <= C|q_h|_1 <= Ch^{-1}||q_h||_0 by the VEM inverse inequality, so the nodal interpolant satisfies ||v-v_I||_0 <= Ch^2|v|_2 <= Ch||q_h||_0 and ||v_I||_1 <= C||q_h||_0 via the existing H^2 interpolation estimates; bound the bubble correction by the moment-based norm equivalence ||d_h||_{1,K} <= Ch_K^{-1}||v-v_I||_{0,K}; finally rescale v_h to enforce the norm equality (constants change accordingly).
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup condition (prop:added-6) is unproven as written; consequently the well-posedness of the discrete problem (prop:added-7, whose proof by adaptation relies on it, and thm:added-2) and the error estimates that invoke well-posedness (thm:est, cor:added-1, thm:added-3) are not established as written.
issues.title: Weak inf-sup proof applies the nodal VEM interpolant to an H^1 lifting and uses estimates outside their hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The statement is very likely true, but repairing the proof requires a contained nontrivial modification (a regularized divergence lifting with H^2 control plus inverse inequalities and bubble norm estimates) rather than a short routine fix; the weak inf-sup and all downstream results survive unchanged, so no major loss or new global architecture is involved.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\u_I$ is the interpolant of $\u$ in $\enhancedunoG\subset\V_k$ and $p_I$ is the interpolant of $p$ in $Q_k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The convergence analysis approximates pressures with the nodal/moment VEM interpolant even when the function is only H^1. In thm:est the pressure approximant is 'the interpolant p_I of p in Q_k', and cor:added-1 invokes it with p in H^k(Omega); for the MINI case k=1 -- the paper's principal case -- H^1(Omega) does not embed into C^0(Omega) in two dimensions, so the vertex values defining p_I do not exist and the needed bound ||p-p_I||_0 <= Ch|p|_1 is unavailable from nodal interpolation. The identical defect occurs in the duality argument of thm:added-3: the dual pressure only satisfies rho in H^1(Omega) (sharp Stokes regularity on a convex polygon), yet the proof uses its nodal interpolant rho_I in eq:interp_dual and in the subsequent terms (eq:IV-eq:VI).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the nodal interpolants p_I and rho_I by a standard Clement-type quasi-interpolant into the enhanced VEM space (H^1-stable with ||p-p_I||_0 <= Ch^k|p|_k for p in H^k, as available in the VEM literature); the proofs of thm:est and thm:added-3 use only that p_I, rho_I belong to Q_k, so they go through verbatim and all statements and rates survive.
issues.overall_effect: For k=1 the optimal pressure estimate of cor:added-1 is not established as written, and the L^2 velocity estimate of thm:added-3 (for every k) is not established as written, since both proofs rely on nodal interpolants of merely H^1 pressures.
issues.title: Nodal pressure interpolants used for merely H^1 functions (k=1 pressure estimate in cor:added-1; dual pressure in thm:added-3)
issues.why_classification: The repair is a routine, local replacement of the approximant by a standard quasi-interpolant; no statement, rate, or advertised regime is lost and no new nontrivial lemma is required.
